text: Do not hand-edit generated artifacts (e.g. `robots.docs.txt`, `tools/release-data.json`); regenerate them by running the corresponding generator/management command (e.g. `python manage_translations.py robots_txt`, `python generate_release_roadmap.py --first-release <version> --date <YYYY-MM>`) so the committed output always matches what the generator produces.
reason: Hand-editing generated files causes the checked-in artifact to drift from the generator, yielding stale, incomplete, or duplicated output (e.g. missing locales below the translation threshold) that is silently overwritten on the next regeneration.
common_pattern: Generated artifacts must never be hand-edited or committed as static output; they must always be produced by running their generator/management command so the checked-in content stays consistent with the source of truth.

text: Control layout alignment and spacing with CSS flexbox properties on the flex container/items (e.g., `justify-content`, `gap`, `align-self`, or auto margins) rather than presentational hacks such as `float` on flex children or empty spacer elements in the template.
reason: Mixing floats with flexbox causes conflicting/unpredictable layout, and empty spacer markup is non-semantic; keeping layout concerns in CSS makes templates cleaner and easier to maintain.
common_pattern: CSS-driven layout: use flexbox alignment/distribution properties (and inline-block-safe auto margins) instead of presentational hacks like floats, empty spacer elements, or non-functional centering declarations.

text: Horizontal auto margins (`margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto`) only take effect on block-level elements, so pair them with `display: block` (or another block-level display mode) — otherwise the centering declarations silently do nothing on inline elements like ``.
reason: Auto horizontal margins are ignored on inline elements, so centering appears to work in intent but has no effect; setting `display: block` makes the declaration functional.
common_pattern: CSS-driven layout: use flexbox alignment/distribution properties (and inline-block-safe auto margins) instead of presentational hacks like floats, empty spacer elements, or non-functional centering declarations.

text: When enumerating platform-specific content variant classes (e.g. `c-content-win` or `.c-content-win`), include all sibling platform variants (e.g. `c-content-unix` / `.c-content-unix`) in the same SCSS selector list or JavaScript condition so all platform variants receive consistent styling and behavior.
reason: Prevents platform-specific gaps where one OS content class is styled or handled while a sibling OS class is omitted, causing inconsistent behavior or missing styles across platforms.
scope: project-wide SCSS selector lists and JS class checks involving platform-specific content variants such as `.c-content-*`
common_pattern: Platform-specific content variant classes must be handled as a complete set: when one OS variant is referenced, all sibling OS variants should be included in the same styling or behavioral condition.

text: In HTML templates, use semantic list elements that match the content: `<ul>`/`<ol>` with `<li>` for groups of similar items, and `<dl>` with `<dt>`/`<dd>` for term/definition or name/description pairs. Avoid generic `<div>` containers, heading tags used for visual styling inside list items, and presentational classes on lists; ensure each `<dt>` has a corresponding `<dd>`.
reason: Semantic markup improves accessibility, document structure, machine readability, and default styling, and avoids abusing generic containers or heading tags for presentation.
common_pattern: Use semantically appropriate HTML list markup in templates instead of generic containers or presentational markup, including correct term/description pairing in definition lists.

text: In user-facing templates, use consistent punctuation across sibling bulleted list items. In checklist templates specifically, do not end bullet items with a period.
reason: Inconsistent punctuation across sibling list items looks like an oversight and reduces the polish of the rendered page; matching the existing checklist style avoids inconsistent punctuation in rendered release checklists.
scope: global (template files), with the no-period convention applying to checklist templates
common_pattern: Punctuation/format consistency in user-facing template files: sibling bulleted items in templates (including checklists) should use consistent punctuation, with the project convention being no trailing period on checklist items. A third generalization (checklist content should match the project's actual formats, e.g., markdown vs reStructuredText) is only superficially related — it concerns factual accuracy of template content rather than punctuation consistency.

text: When programmatically moving the viewport (e.g. `window.scrollTo`, `element.focus()` followed by `scrollIntoView()`), use the DOM API's options-object form to make scroll behavior explicit and correct: pass `{ top, left, behavior: 'smooth' }` to `scrollTo` to preserve existing smooth scrolling instead of the positional `(x, y)` form, and pass `{ preventScroll: true }` to `focus()` when another call (e.g. `scrollIntoView`) is responsible for scrolling, to avoid competing viewport scrolls. Avoid positional/naked-argument calls that silently change behavior to an instant jump.
reason: Positional `scrollTo(x, y)` cannot express a scroll behavior and causes an unintended regression from smooth to instant scrolling; likewise `focus()` without `preventScroll: true` competes with `scrollIntoView()`, producing a jump to the top followed by a second smooth scroll. The options-object form preserves UX and matches MDN-documented usage.
common_pattern: When calling DOM APIs that manipulate the viewport scroll position (scrollTo, focus, scrollIntoView), use the options-object form so scroll behavior is explicit and intentional, instead of positional/naked-argument calls that silently produce instant jumps or competing scrolls.

text: Write data migrations (migrations that alter data via RunPython) as separate migration files rather than combining them with schema changes in the same migration.
reason: Django recommends this, and combining schema changes with RunPython operations can cause errors such as `OperationalError: cannot ALTER TABLE ... because it has pending trigger events` on databases that support DDL transactions (SQLite, PostgreSQL).
common_pattern: Django migration best practices — managing the content, naming, purpose, and PR-scope of migration files so migration history stays intentional and clean

text: Use standard Python comment syntax (`# `) for explanatory comments instead of Sphinx-style `#:` prefixes.
reason: Keeps comments consistent with ordinary Python style and avoids implying special documentation semantics where none are intended.
common_pattern: Comment hygiene: comments should carry information the code cannot (non-obvious intent, constraints, magic values), be placed with the code they explain, and follow standard syntax. Six of nine generalizations converge on the 'do not restate / do not document change history' half, and one (Gen 7) supplies the complementary 'do document non-obvious magic values' half.

text: In Django templates, format dates and times using Django's localization-aware formatting machinery: named format constants (e.g., DATE_FORMAT, TIME_FORMAT, DATETIME_FORMAT, MONTH_DAY_FORMAT), the date filter, timezone filters (e.g., utc), and centrally defined formats.py. Avoid hardcoded format strings, manual component concatenation, and model properties that duplicate built-in template filters. Choose the format constant matching the needed precision (e.g., use 'Y' for year-only rather than YEAR_MONTH_FORMAT), and bind repeated filtered values with {% with %}.
reason: Hardcoded date/time formats are not localizable and produce US-centric output; Django's named formats and filters respect the active locale and project settings, while model properties duplicating template filters add unnecessary surface area.
common_pattern: Django template date/time rendering should use Django's localization-aware machinery—named format constants, date/timezone filters, and centrally defined formats.py—rather than hardcoded English/US format strings, manual component concatenation, or model properties that duplicate built-in filters.

text: Avoid gratuitous whitespace in template files: no trailing whitespace, no unnecessary blank lines, and keep adjacent block elements (e.g. a heading and its following paragraph) directly next to each other.
reason: Blank lines and trailing whitespace have no rendering effect, create spurious diff noise, and may introduce unintended trailing whitespace.
common_pattern: Whitespace and newline handling in template files: whitespace is noise in diffs for all templates, and is semantically significant (visible output) in text/plain templates.

text: For direction-sensitive UI, use writing-direction-aware primitives instead of hardcoded physical directions: prefer CSS logical properties (`inline-start`/`inline-end`, `block-start`/`block-end`) over physical keywords (`left`/`right`/`top`/`bottom`), and verify directional glyphs/icons (e.g., arrows) render correctly for the target reading order.
reason: Physical direction values and hardcoded arrow directions do not mirror for RTL languages, causing layout and iconography to remain directionally incorrect.
common_pattern: Direction-aware / RTL-safe UI implementation: avoid hardcoded physical direction assumptions and use writing-direction-aware alternatives.

text: Text files should end with exactly one trailing newline: ensure a single newline (LF) after the last content line, and remove any trailing blank lines.
reason: This merges the complementary requirements (must have a trailing newline; must not have multiple trailing blank lines) into a single end-of-file convention. It follows POSIX convention, avoids '\ No newline at end of file' diff noise, satisfies linters/editorconfig, and keeps diffs clean.
common_pattern: Both generalizations specify the correct end-of-file formatting for text files: exactly one trailing newline, with no additional blank lines.

text: Use the standard unprefixed CSS property as the canonical declaration, with vendor-prefixed variants (e.g. `-webkit-*`, `-moz-*`) added only as a supplement — never as a replacement. Likewise, remove obsolete Modernizr-style feature-detection fallback classes (e.g. `.mdzr-no-X`) once the detected feature is universally supported by the project's target browsers.
reason: Reduces dead weight and noise while ensuring standards-based behavior and compatibility with browsers that support the unprefixed property (and future-proofing as prefixes are dropped).
common_pattern: Progressive-enhancement / browser-compatibility hygiene for CSS: prefer standard, standards-based declarations over legacy compatibility workarounds, and validate new feature usage against target browsers.

text: When building URLs from a base URL (e.g. from settings/config) and dynamic values, use `urllib.parse` helpers instead of string formatting or concatenation: `urljoin()` to join path segments onto the base URL, and `urlencode()`/`quote()` to encode user-derived query-parameter values before inserting them.
reason: The base URL may gain or lose a trailing slash and dynamic values may contain reserved characters (space, `&`, `?`, `#`), producing malformed URLs or enabling query-parameter injection; the standard helpers normalize and escape safely.
common_pattern: Both generalizations address safe URL construction in Python: replacing naive string formatting/concatenation with standard `urllib.parse` helpers (urljoin for joining base URLs with path segments, urlencode/quote for encoding query values) to avoid malformed URLs and injection issues.

text: In `djangoproject/scss/_style.scss`, create visual separation between stacked sections by reusing existing design primitives: add `border-top: 1px solid $black` to page sections such as `#billboard` when a top border is needed, but for `.full-width` blocks rely on the existing `box-shadow` and do not add or retain `border-bottom`.
reason: Maintains visual hierarchy without extra markup and follows the established SCSS design intent for each layout block.
common_pattern: SCSS visual separation between adjacent/stacked page sections in `djangoproject/scss/_style.scss` should reuse existing design primitives, with the appropriate separation technique depending on the component.

text: In data migrations, compute derived values from existing model fields programmatically using database expressions (e.g., F, Concat) in a bulk update rather than enumerating a hardcoded literal mapping for every row. If a small number of rows deviate from the formula, apply the formula as the default and define an explicit mapping only for those exceptions.
reason: Avoids large duplicated mappings, keeps migrations concise, and prevents hardcoded data from diverging from model fields while still handling edge cases explicitly.
scope: Django data migrations / mapping-backed data migrations
common_pattern: In data migrations, avoid enumerating hardcoded per-row literal values; instead derive values from existing model fields via database expressions (e.g., F, Concat) in bulk updates, keeping only genuinely exceptional rows as an explicit mapping.

text: In multi-line shell blocks inside Dockerfile `RUN` instructions (e.g., `if ...; then ...; fi`), align control-flow keywords (`if`, `then`, `fi`, `do`, `done`, `esac`) with each other and indent only the body/arguments between them; terminate the final keyword on its own properly terminated line and never leave a trailing line-continuation backslash after it.
reason: A stray `\` after a keyword like `fi` acts as an unintended line continuation that swallows the next line or produces a malformed command, and an indented keyword is easily misread as a package name or argument, inviting incorrect edits.
common_pattern: Formatting and terminating shell control-flow keywords (`if`/`then`/`fi`, etc.) correctly within multi-line Dockerfile `RUN` blocks so keywords are visually distinguishable from package arguments and never produce stray line continuations.

text: In Django ORM queries, when a computed expression is needed only in filters (or would otherwise be duplicated), define it once with `.alias(name=expression)` and reference the alias in subsequent `.filter()` calls instead of using `.annotate()` or inlining the expression.
reason: `.alias()` keeps derived values out of returned model instances while still making them available for filtering, reduces duplicated SQL expressions, and improves readability.
common_pattern: Use Django ORM `.alias()` instead of `.annotate()` or inline duplication when a computed expression is needed for filtering and should not appear in the query's SELECT output.

text: For visual effects (e.g., fading, opacity changes), use CSS transitions and let CSS own the timing and final values. JavaScript should only toggle a state class, and if JS must run after a transition, listen for the `transitionend` event instead of using `setTimeout`. In SCSS, co-locate transition/animation declarations with the state or modifier selector that triggers them (e.g., `&.fade-out`).
reason: Keeps presentation logic declarative in CSS, avoids duplicated timing values between CSS and JS, and groups related animation logic for maintainability.
common_pattern: CSS should own transition/animation timing and visual effects; JavaScript should only toggle state classes and listen for transition events rather than duplicating timing, and SCSS should co-locate animation declarations with the triggering selector.

text: When an anchor `id` is needed for accessibility or skip-link targets in templates, attach it to an existing semantic container (e.g. `<main>`) rather than adding an empty `<div>` solely to carry the anchor.
reason: Avoids unnecessary markup, preserves semantic structure, and prevents empty wrapper elements from interfering with visibility or layout of content.
common_pattern: Section headings in site/documentation templates must expose a deep-link anchor whose fragment is the slugified heading text (Django's `plink`/`headerlink` convention), and anchor `id`s must be unique and attached to existing semantic elements rather than empty wrappers.

text: Define search-result highlight delimiters (e.g. START_SEL/STOP_SEL for <mark>/</mark>) as named constants in the search queryset module, and import/reuse those constants from template filters instead of duplicating the markup literals.
reason: Provides a single source of truth for paired highlight tags, prevents drift between search and template-filter code, and makes future markup changes safer.
common_pattern: Extract shared search-result highlight markup delimiters (<mark>/</mark>) into named constants in a single module and reuse them everywhere instead of duplicating literals.

text: Use semantic landmark HTML elements (e.g., <nav>, <search>) instead of generic <div>/<span> containers with ARIA roles for navigation and search regions. When multiple navigation landmarks may appear on a page, give each a unique accessible name via aria-label or aria-labelledby (e.g., 'Primary' or 'Main' for main navigation).
reason: Improves accessibility for screen reader users, reduces reliance on ARIA patches, and disambiguates multiple navigation landmarks.
common_pattern: Accessibility best practices for navigation landmarks: prefer semantic HTML landmark elements over generic <div>/<span> with ARIA roles, and provide accessible labels when multiple navigation landmarks may appear.

text: Centralize search-related definitions: define search option keys/labels as a single mapping in `search.py`, and expose per-searchable-view values such as `template_name`, `absolute_url`, and rendered `html` as attributes or properties on the view class (e.g. `SearchableView`). Reference these definitions from views, templates, and sync code instead of duplicating literals or computing them at call sites.
reason: Keeps validation, filtering, UI labels, templates, and derived view data synchronized, avoids drift, and makes each searchable view self-contained.
common_pattern: Avoid duplicated literals and call-site computation by giving shared definitions a single authoritative owner—module-level mappings for search options, and view-class attributes/properties for per-view configuration and derived values—then referencing those definitions from consumers.

text: When the same regex literal is used in multiple branches or locations, extract it into a named variable or constant and reuse that name instead of repeating the literal.
reason: Creates a single source of truth for the pattern, makes future edits safer, and lets the variable name document the pattern's purpose.
common_pattern: Consolidating repeated text-normalization and regex logic into a single reusable construct rather than duplicating operations or literals.

text:
In Django form templates, render fields using Django's built-in helpers instead of hardcoding IDs or manually reconstructing markup: use `{{ form..id_for_label }}` (or `{{ form..label_tag }}`) for label/input binding rather than hardcoded `id_`, and prefer `{{ form..as_field_group }}` wrapped in a `
` over manually rendering each field's label, errors, and input. Keep the surrounding structure consistent (e.g., wrap the submit button container in a `
`, not a `

`, when field groups use `

`).
reason: Django's form helpers stay in sync with generated IDs, form prefixes, and custom widgets, avoid duplicating Django's ID/label generation logic in templates, and consolidate field rendering to remove boilerplate and prevent invalid nested block elements.
common_pattern: Django form templates should leverage Django's built-in form rendering helpers (id_for_label, label_tag, as_field_group) rather than hardcoding generated IDs or manually reconstructing label/error markup, and should render form-level errors (non_field_errors) that Django emits outside individual fields.

text: In search-result templates, design the zero-results state so that filter/navigation controls remain above the results count (visible when there are no results), and the empty-state message does not repeat the adjacent heading but instead offers a forward action, such as a link to broaden the search.
reason: Filters remain useful in the empty state, and a non-redundant, actionable message turns a dead-end zero-results page into a recoverable one.
scope: search-result UI templates, especially the zero-results state
common_pattern: Zero-results search UX: keep filter/navigation controls visible even when no results are returned, and make the empty-state message non-redundant and actionable.

text: In HTML templates, keep labels and accessible names non-redundant: show form labels that provide useful visible context instead of hiding them with visuallyhidden; for icon-only controls, use visually hidden text that describes the action rather than repeating the associated field label; and remove nested span.visuallyhidden text when an aria-label already supplies the same accessible name.
reason: Reduces duplicate screen-reader announcements and preserves useful visible affordances for sighted users.
common_pattern: Accessible label hygiene in HTML templates: avoid redundant or needlessly hidden label text, while preserving labels that provide useful visible context.

text: In HTML/Django templates, decorative images/icons must be explicitly hidden from assistive technology: use `alt=""` on decorative `` elements and either a non-semantic `` or `aria-hidden="true"` on decorative icons. Do not add descriptive alt text when adjacent visible text already conveys the image’s meaning; verify the decision against actual screen-reader behavior.
reason: Decorative images and icons otherwise create screen-reader noise or trigger accessibility-checker violations. Empty alt text and aria-hidden are the standard ways to mark elements as decorative, and redundant translated alt text adds maintenance burden without an accessibility benefit.
common_pattern: Accessibility handling of decorative images/icons in templates: explicitly hide decorative elements from assistive technology via empty alt text or aria-hidden, and avoid adding redundant descriptive alt text when surrounding text already conveys the meaning.

text: When creating multiple instances of the same model, use Model.objects.bulk_create([...]) instead of repeated .create() calls, including in test setup and inside loops. If the created objects are needed for later relations or assertions, keep the returned objects.
reason: Reduces repeated database round-trips, avoids boilerplate, and keeps bulk fixture or sync setup concise.
common_pattern: Batch-create multiple instances of the same model with bulk_create() instead of issuing repeated individual create() calls. The cluster spans test fixture setup and production sync/loop contexts.

text: In `docs/builder.py`, wrap tuples returned by `domain.get_objects()` in a `DomainObject` dataclass with named fields (`name`, `dispname`, `type`, `docname`, `anchor`, `priority`), and expose any derived values (e.g., `code_path`) as properties on that dataclass instead of computing them inline in the builder.
reason: Makes Sphinx domain object data self-documenting, avoids error-prone tuple index access, and keeps domain-specific derivation with the domain object so builder methods are easier to read and maintain.
common_pattern: Encapsulate Sphinx domain object data in a dedicated `DomainObject` dataclass within `docs/builder.py`, using named fields and properties for derived values to improve readability and reduce inline tuple manipulation.

text: In Python code, prefer pathlib.Path idioms over string/os.path manipulation: compose paths with the `/` operator instead of `Path.joinpath()` or `os.path.join`, use Path methods (`read_text()`, `write_text()`, `path.open()`) instead of `open(path, ...)`, and pass Path objects directly to APIs that accept path-like objects rather than casting them with `str()`.
reason: pathlib provides a clearer, platform-independent, and more concise path API; operational methods like `write_text()`/`read_text()` eliminate file-handle boilerplate and indentation, the `/` operator is more readable than `joinpath()`, and Path accepts path-like objects so `str()` casting is redundant.
common_pattern: Prefer idiomatic pathlib.Path usage in Python: use the `/` operator for path joining, use Path convenience methods (read_text/write_text/open) for file I/O, and pass Path objects directly instead of converting via str()/os.path.

text: When deriving an absolute path from `__file__`, apply `.parent` before `.resolve()` (e.g., `Path(__file__).parent.resolve()`) instead of resolving the file first.
reason: `.parent` is independent of `.resolve()`, and `.resolve()` should be applied as a post-operation to the directory path being made absolute.
common_pattern: Prefer idiomatic pathlib.Path usage in Python: use the `/` operator for path joining, use Path convenience methods (read_text/write_text/open) for file I/O, and pass Path objects directly instead of converting via str()/os.path.

text: In `docs/templates/docs/search_results.html`, when a condition special-cases a known code-reference prefix (e.g., `term-`), handle all supported sibling prefixes (e.g., `envvar-`) in the same branch instead of letting them fall through to the default.
reason: Prevents inconsistent rendering and lost formatting for recognized code references.
common_pattern: Consistency in special-casing known code-reference prefixes for display logic in documentation search templates.

text: Prefer `dataclass` instances with named fields over tuples or positionally-accessed sequences when representing multi-field structured data, especially when extracting data out of usage logic or consuming external APIs. When mapping tuple-valued results into a dataclass, unpack each tuple into the constructor (e.g., `Dataclass(*item)` or `starmap(Dataclass, items)`) rather than passing the tuple as one positional argument. If the extracted dataclass or constant becomes verbose, place it in a dedicated module rather than alongside the consuming code.
reason: Named dataclass fields improve readability and self-documentation, avoid brittle positional indexing, prevent `TypeError` from passing a tuple as a single constructor argument, and keep configuration/data separate from usage logic.
common_pattern: Prefer dataclasses with named fields over tuples or positional-argument data structures for multi-field data, including when consuming external API results and when extracting data out of usage logic.

text: When a DOM enhancement must apply to multiple markup variants or duplicated elements, handle them uniformly rather than special-casing one: model the variants as data-driven config entries (e.g. { selector, getContainer, getText } callbacks) and update all matching elements together, instead of hardcoding one selector and generic traversal or adding a helper to pick the single visible instance.
reason: Keeps the handler simple and extensible: new markup variants or duplicated elements (e.g. desktop and mobile layouts) can be supported without changing core behavior or risking a missed element.
scope: DOM enhancement scripts that manipulate multiple markup variants or repeated elements
common_pattern: DOM enhancement logic should handle multiple markup variants / matching elements uniformly (via data-driven config or bulk updates) instead of special-casing a single selector or the single visible/active element.

text: In frontend JavaScript, for static or trusted content, prefer assigning directly via `innerText` for plain text and `innerHTML` for trusted markup instead of manually creating nodes with `document.createTextNode`, `document.createElement`, and `appendChild`. Never use `innerHTML` with user-controlled or dynamically composed strings without sanitization.
reason: Direct content assignment is simpler, more concise, and avoids unnecessary DOM-construction boilerplate for fixed/trusted content. The `innerHTML` caveat prevents XSS when the content is not trusted.
common_pattern: Prefer direct DOM content-assignment APIs over manual DOM node construction for simple, trusted/static frontend content, while preserving safety constraints for untrusted content.

text: Scope CSS rules to the nearest component container class: avoid adding unnecessary top-level page/section ancestor prefixes (which raise specificity and make overrides harder), and before hoisting a generic selector (e.g. `span.title`) out of component scope, verify no unrelated elements elsewhere match it — otherwise keep it scoped.
reason: Lower specificity keeps styles easy to override for specific applications, and component-scoped selectors prevent unintentionally styling unrelated elements elsewhere on the site.
common_pattern: Both generalizations concern CSS selector scoping in component styles: prefer the narrowest selector scope (nearest component container, component-scoped generic selectors) and avoid unnecessary ancestor prefixes or globalized selectors that raise specificity and risk styling unrelated elements.

text: When persisting Django model instances, perform save operations in the correct order: set all known field values before the initial save/create rather than creating the row and immediately updating it, and ensure the instance has been saved (has a primary key) before calling `save_m2m()` or otherwise saving many-to-many relations.
reason: This avoids redundant database writes and prevents failures when saving many-to-many relations on an unsaved instance.
common_pattern: Correct ordering of Django ORM persistence operations: set known values before the initial save, and ensure the instance is persisted before saving dependent relations.

text: Use early-return guard clauses to reduce nesting in conditionals and event handlers, handling preconditions up front instead of nesting the main logic in an if block. Document non-obvious early-return conditions with a brief comment.
reason: Flat control flow is more readable and maintainable; guard clauses keep the main logic at the top level, and brief comments explain non-obvious domain-specific exits.
common_pattern: Early-return guard clauses to reduce nesting, with documentation for non-obvious exit conditions.

reason:
Headings are navigable by screen readers and assistive technology, while

common_pattern:

text: In CSS/SCSS, use the most concise valid shorthand for margin/padding: collapse equal left/right values into the 2- or 3-value form instead of repeating the fourth value.
reason: Reduces redundancy and makes it clear which sides share spacing values.
common_pattern: CSS/SCSS spacing declaration hygiene: concise shorthand and intentional numeric magnitudes.

text: When setting CSS/SCSS spacing values, verify numeric magnitudes are intentional and plausible for the layout; large decimal values such as `10.5em` may be typos for smaller values like `1.5em`.
reason: Unintentionally large margins or paddings can break page layout and often indicate a typo.
common_pattern: CSS/SCSS spacing declaration hygiene: concise shorthand and intentional numeric magnitudes.

text: In template/HTML files, write long href URLs on a single line without backslash-newline continuations or multi-line wrapping, so the URL value remains complete and syntactically valid.
reason: Wrapping long URLs can introduce whitespace, backslashes, or other unintended characters into the attribute value, corrupting links and making updates harder.
common_pattern: Long URLs in template/HTML href attributes must remain syntactically intact and should not be wrapped or continued across lines.

text: Define JavaScript constructors and prototype-based objects using ES6 `class` syntax instead of function-constructor plus prototype-assignment patterns.
reason: Class syntax is more modern, idiomatic, and clearer, and it better supports inheritance and static analysis.
common_pattern: Both generalizations prescribe the same JavaScript idiom preference: use ES6 `class` syntax for defining constructors and prototype-based objects, rather than function-constructor + prototype-assignment patterns. They differ only in incidental wording, not in substance.

text: Prefer element-wise iteration constructs (`for...of` for arrays, `.forEach()` for collections such as `document.querySelectorAll(...)` results — converting non-iterable collections with `Array.from(...)` when needed) over index-based C-style `for` loops whenever the index is not otherwise required.
reason: Element-wise iteration is more concise, avoids manual index management and off-by-one errors, and reads more clearly when only the elements (not the index) are needed.
common_pattern: Prefer element-wise iteration abstractions (`for...of`, `.forEach()`) over manual index-based C-style `for` loops when the index itself is not required.

text: For Django settings and static configuration values, use collection literals that match usage: tuples for fixed ordered sequences (e.g., `LOCALE_PATHS`), set literals for unordered membership checks (e.g., `{'POST'}`), and only use `frozenset` when immutability or hashability is actually required.
reason: Expresses immutability and order-independence, optimizes membership checks, and avoids visual noise from unnecessary wrappers.
common_pattern: Choosing appropriate collection types for static configuration values to express intent (immutability, membership) and avoid unnecessary wrappers.

text: In translatable pluralized count messages (e.g. `ngettext`, Django `{% blocktranslate count ... %}`), always interpolate the count variable/placeholder such as `%(count)d` or `{{ num_results }}` into both the singular and plural forms instead of hardcoding `1`, and avoid count-specific qualifiers like "Only" that assume the count is exactly 1.
reason: Plural rules differ across languages; some languages use the singular form for counts other than 1, so hardcoding the count or using "only one"-style qualifiers prevents correct localization.
common_pattern: i18n-safe interpolation in translatable numeric messages: keep count and unit variables as placeholders inside translation strings, and avoid hardcoded literals or qualifiers that assume English grammar or unambiguous units

text: When interpolating a numeric value with a unit (for example a percentage) into user-facing text, include the explicit unit word or symbol such as "percent" or "%" inside the same translatable string as the placeholder, rather than concatenating it outside the translation, so the number is unambiguous and translators can order the value and unit correctly.
reason: Without an in-string unit, values like "0" or "50" may be read as absolute counts, and units appended outside the translation block cannot be reordered correctly across locales.
common_pattern: i18n-safe interpolation in translatable numeric messages: keep count and unit variables as placeholders inside translation strings, and avoid hardcoded literals or qualifiers that assume English grammar or unambiguous units

text: Before removing a model field, method, function, or custom QuerySet/manager method, search for its references across the file/module/codebase; delete it only if it is no longer used anywhere, and delete it promptly once confirmed unused rather than leaving dead code behind.
reason: Unreferenced members are dead code that raises maintenance cost and misleads developers about available fields/filters (and can leave stale database schema assumptions when fields are involved), while deleting a still-referenced member breaks callers and causes runtime errors. Together these require confirming unused status before deletion and removing confirmed dead code.
common_pattern: Dead-code lifecycle discipline: verify a member has no remaining references before removing it, and remove it once it is confirmed unused.

text: Static and generated SVG assets should use a transparent background so they blend with the surrounding page/theme, and should reuse the exact color values from their source-of-truth component (e.g., the mirroring JS module's palette) instead of introducing approximate hex values.
reason: Hardcoded backgrounds assume a theme and clash with the real page background, and near-miss colors (e.g., #d9185c vs #d9195c) are visually undetectable yet break consistency and the single source of truth.
common_pattern: Color handling in static/generated SVG assets and themeable logo/icon areas: assets should match their true source-of-truth palette (JS module, theme tokens) rather than hardcoding approximated colors, and color choices (transparency vs. fixed vs. themeable) must respect the surrounding theme and remain legible across light/dark modes.

text: When swapping a fixed (light) color for a themeable token in logo/icon areas, verify foreground contrast across light and dark modes; keep colors that are intentionally fixed as literal hex values rather than interpolating theme variables.
reason: Theme tokens resolve differently per mode, so foregrounds can lose contrast (dark-on-dark logos), while intentionally-fixed styling should stay independent of configurable palettes.
common_pattern: Color handling in static/generated SVG assets and themeable logo/icon areas: assets should match their true source-of-truth palette (JS module, theme tokens) rather than hardcoding approximated colors, and color choices (transparency vs. fixed vs. themeable) must respect the surrounding theme and remain legible across light/dark modes.

text: In SVG/Jinja templates, follow readability-focused conventions: format multi-attribute elements with one attribute per line using consistent indentation, annotate conditional blocks with HTML comments identifying their rendered element or role, and style text elements using named CSS classes defined in the <style> block (choosing by visual typography rather than semantic role name).
reason: Improves readability, maintainability, and reviewability of SVG templates; centralizes typography and avoids duplicating font declarations.
common_pattern: SVG/Jinja template formatting and styling conventions for readability and maintainability

text: In tools/generate_release_roadmap.py, keep SVG roadmap layout tuning values (e.g., pixels_per_year, bar_height, bar_v_spacing, legend_box_size, legend_padding, font_size) as named entries in the module-level CONFIG dict instead of hardcoding them inline; adjust related layout values together. For example, font_size should be a CONFIG entry set to 18 for readability.
reason: Centralizing presentation constants makes generated SVG elements easier to adjust consistently and avoids cramped or uneven layouts and inline hardcoding.
common_pattern: Visual/SVG roadmap layout constants should be centralized as named entries in a module-level CONFIG mapping rather than hardcoded inline, and related layout values should be tuned together.

text: For chart/timeline grid generation (e.g., SVG templates such as `tools/template.svg.jinja`), model axis labels explicitly: define repeated label mappings as named constants (e.g., `FIRST_YEAR_MONTH_LABELS`), represent grid-line annotations with separate optional `top_label` and `bottom_label` fields rather than a single shared `label` field, render each label conditionally at its corresponding top/bottom padding boundary, and render repeating period labels only once (e.g., month labels only in the first year block) while still repeating year labels on each year's first line.
reason: This merges the complementary data-model and template-rendering halves while preserving the project-specific label-mapping and repetition conventions that improve clarity and reduce visual clutter in timeline charts.
scope: SVG chart/grid templates, especially timeline/chart label generation
common_pattern: Explicit modeling and conditional rendering of axis labels in chart/timeline grid generation.

text: In generated roadmap graphics, use compact and stable display labels—such as abbreviated month names with periods and year-only labels for calver releases—rather than full names that may crowd the chart or become misleading over time.
reason: Roadmap SVG labels are long-lived and space-constrained; compact, stable labels remain readable and accurate for the chart's lifetime.
common_pattern: Release-roadmap generation and rendering should be metadata-driven and use durable, compact display representations, avoiding hardcoded static lists, relative timing phrases, and full names that can become stale or crowded.

text: Prefer the native `Element.checkVisibility()` API over custom element-visibility helpers (e.g., `isVisible`, `el.offsetParent !== null`) when the project's supported-browser baseline includes it, removing the custom helper and updating its call sites accordingly.
reason: Native browser APIs reduce custom utility code, rely on browser-maintained behavior, and simplify call sites. Checking the supported-browser baseline first ensures the native API is actually available where the code runs.
common_pattern: Both generalizations recommend replacing hand-rolled element-visibility helpers (e.g., `isVisible`, `el.offsetParent !== null`) with the native `Element.checkVisibility()` API, justified by the project's supported-browser baseline. The second is a direct restatement of the first with a concrete code example, so they converge on a single principle.

text: In SVG timeline templates (e.g., `tools/template.svg.jinja`), bar `<rect>` elements must explicitly set `stroke="{{ colors.<bar_type> }}"` (matching the bar's type color, such as `colors.mainstream` for mainstream/extended-release bars) and a fixed `stroke-width` (e.g., `2`) — do not rely on fill alone to distinguish bars from the background.
reason: An explicit outline makes bar elements distinguishable from the background and lets shared stroke colors encode relationships between bar segments (e.g., extended release bars keyed to the mainstream color).
common_pattern: SVG timeline bar `<rect>` elements must explicitly set `stroke` (using the corresponding palette color) and a fixed `stroke-width` so bar outlines are rendered deliberately rather than relying on fill alone.

text: When changing an element's tag for semantic or accessibility reasons, update the corresponding CSS selectors and reset or override browser default styles as needed so the existing visual design is preserved.
reason: Native/semantic elements may have different default browser styling and may no longer match existing CSS selectors, causing visual or layout regressions if not explicitly handled.
common_pattern: Changing an element's tag for semantic or accessibility reasons requires updating its CSS so the existing visual design and browser-default styling behavior are preserved.

text: When applying an accessibility fix (e.g., adding `tabindex="0"` or adjusting focus/contrast styles), first verify the selector's scope matches the element the ticket actually targets (e.g., a logo nested under `.footer` vs. the main navbar logo), rather than a similarly-named element elsewhere; once the correct target is confirmed, apply the identical change consistently across all analogous templates/components that share the same UI pattern.
reason: Applying a fix to the wrong (but similarly-named) element leaves the reported issue unresolved and may introduce unintended changes, while applying it to only one of several duplicated templates creates inconsistent accessibility behavior wherever the component is rendered.
common_pattern: Scoping accessibility fixes: identify the correct target element/selector, then apply the change consistently across analogous occurrences

text: For keyboard accessibility, prefer native HTML semantics and explicit state over focus hacks: use natively focusable/interactive elements such as <a> and <button> instead of adding tabindex="0" to focusable elements or non-interactive containers, and reveal dropdown/menu contents via an explicit open state (e.g. an &.open class toggled on activation) rather than CSS :focus-within.
reason: This keeps focus order predictable, avoids redundant or fragile tabindex management, and prevents keyboard users from being forced through hidden menu items before reaching subsequent controls.
common_pattern: Keyboard accessibility should rely on native HTML semantics and explicit interactive state rather than redundant tabindex attributes or CSS-driven focus expansion.

text: In static browser-only JavaScript files (e.g. under `djangoproject/static/js/`), do not add new top-level global functions or variables; define helpers inside the existing IIFE, handler, or module scope where they are used.
reason: Static JS files that historically add nothing to the global namespace should preserve that encapsulation, avoid namespace collisions, and enable helper reuse without polluting globals.
common_pattern: Project-specific conventions for managing global scope and global-object access in browser-only static JavaScript files.

text: In browser-only static JavaScript, prefer environment-appropriate browser globals such as `window` for global object access; use `globalThis` only when the code actually needs to run across multiple JavaScript environments.
reason: The repository's front-end code is browser-only, so `window` matches the intended runtime and avoids unnecessary cross-environment indirection, but `globalThis` is appropriate if portability across JS runtimes is an explicit requirement.
common_pattern: Project-specific conventions for managing global scope and global-object access in browser-only static JavaScript files.

text: In release checklist templates, make release-workflow distinctions explicit: guard phase- or type-specific items (e.g., pre-release-only steps) with conditionals such as `{% if release.is_pre_release %}` and place the mutually exclusive alternative in an `{% else %}` branch rather than using an unconditional or negatively guarded item; likewise, keep separate section headers for distinct release phases/actions (e.g., feature freeze vs. alpha release) even when they usually occur on the same day, so the checklist reflects the true sequencing.
reason: Prevents pre-release-only steps from leaking into patch/bugfix releases, keeps mutually exclusive release-day steps together in one conditional, and preserves the logical separation of release actions that may occur on different days.
common_pattern: Release checklist templates must keep the semantic distinctions of the release workflow explicit rather than flattening them — phase/type-specific items are guarded by conditionals, and distinct release phases retain their own section headers.

text: Reuse the project's existing focus-indicator style (e.g., the footer's `outline: 2px solid var(--menu)`) for new focus states; do not introduce new outline colors, `outline-offset` values, or `!important` variations, and do not alter already-working focus styles as part of an unrelated change.
reason: Keeps focus states visually consistent across components, avoids one-off styling that drifts over time, and keeps changes scoped to the task at hand.
common_pattern: All three generalizations concern CSS focus-indicator styling: they converge on reusing the project's established focus style (e.g., the footer's `outline: 2px solid var(--menu)`) rather than introducing new outline colors, offsets, `!important`, or unrelated tweaks to already-working focus states.

text: In Django documentation code examples, follow PEP 8 formatting, including two blank lines between top-level class definitions and following top-level statements (e.g., admin.site.register calls).
reason: Django docs use PEP 8 style; consistent blank-line spacing improves readability and matches surrounding documentation conventions.
common_pattern: Django documentation code examples should follow PEP 8 spacing, especially two blank lines between top-level class definitions and following top-level statements such as admin.site.register calls.

text: In members templates, when rendering a member image, use the thumbnail-with-logo fallback pattern: check that `obj.thumbnail` exists before using `obj.thumbnail.url`, otherwise fall back to `obj.logo.url`. Also render the model's existing logo/image field rather than omitting it from the member output.
reason: Prevents template errors from accessing an unset thumbnail URL, makes use of existing model data, and keeps member-listing image rendering consistent across templates.
common_pattern: Rendering member images in Django templates: display the model-provided image/logo, and when both thumbnail and logo may exist, use the thumbnail with a guarded fallback to the logo.

text: Flatten nested `with` statements into a single `with` statement with comma-separated context managers when the context managers are directly nested and independent (ruff SIM117).
reason: Combining multiple context managers into one `with` statement minimizes indentation depth and improves readability; this is enforced by ruff's SIM117 rule.
common_pattern: Both generalizations state the same code-style principle: nested `with` statements that are independent and directly nested should be flattened into a single `with` statement using comma-separated context managers (ruff SIM117), reducing indentation and improving readability.

text: Centralize version-parsing logic (e.g. `get_version_tuple()`, feature-version derivation) in `releases/utils.py` and have models (`Release.version_tuple`, `Release.feature_version`) and template tags (`releases/templatetags/release_notes.py`) delegate to it instead of duplicating ad-hoc parsing.
reason: Ad-hoc parsing scattered across models and template tags diverges and breaks for calendar versions/pre-releases, producing type errors and links to nonexistent docs; a shared helper keeps parsing reusable, testable, and consistent.
scope: releases app version utilities and template tags
common_pattern: Version-parsing logic for releases must be correct for calendar-style versions (e.g. `2028a1`) and must live in a single shared utility (`releases/utils.py`) rather than being reimplemented in models or template tags.

text: When refactoring documentation notice-box SCSS in `_style.scss` (changeset/versionadded/versionchanged/deprecated notes), consolidate shared container styling onto the shared `div.*` selectors and apply label styling directly to label spans such as `span.versionmodified`/`span.title` instead of using paragraph `font-weight` overrides that must later be undone. Preserve the old `span.title` layout/margin behavior, including the rendering of empty-body notes.
reason: This keeps notice-box styling maintainable by avoiding duplicated/overridden CSS while preventing layout regressions when the markup differs from the legacy `span.title` shape.
common_pattern: Refactoring SCSS for documentation notice boxes (version/deprecated/changeset notes) in `_style.scss`: simplify/consolidate selectors while preserving the visual behavior of legacy `span.title` markup, especially for empty-body notes.

text: When adding CSS margins to separate siblings or nested content, scope them contextually (e.g. use `:not(:only-child)` for sibling-only spacing, and `:first-child`/`:last-child` resets for nested elements) so standalone elements and container edges do not receive unwanted extra whitespace.
reason: Spacing intended for sibling separation can create incorrect extra gaps when the styled element is the only child or when content meets the edge of a bounded container.
common_pattern: CSS spacing margins should be conditionally scoped so they only apply where separation is actually needed, avoiding unwanted extra whitespace on sole children and at container edges.

text: For password-hasher migrations in `accounts/hashers.py`, reuse the underlying hasher (e.g. `PBKDF2PasswordHasher`) directly instead of adding wrapper methods like `PBKDF2WrappedSHA1PasswordHasher.encode_sha1_hash` that duplicate encoding logic; only keep the wrapper when the migration cannot import the original hasher.
reason: Avoids unnecessary custom code and duplicated encoding logic, while preserving migration-specific import constraints.
common_pattern: Avoid duplicating password hasher encoding logic in migration-specific wrapper methods; reuse the existing hasher directly unless the migration cannot import it.

text: When writing CSS, verify that selector IDs/classes exactly match the identifiers used in markup and that property names are spelled correctly; use kebab-case for multi-word IDs/classes (e.g., `#back-to-top` rather than `#backtotop`). Invalid or mismatched CSS names are silently ignored, so validate compiled CSS when styling does not apply as expected.
reason: Typos in CSS selectors or properties and mismatched selector identifiers do not produce browser errors, making the resulting styling bugs hard to detect. Following kebab-case also matches CSS naming conventions and improves readability.
common_pattern: CSS identifier/property names must be correct and conventional, because invalid or mismatched CSS names fail silently and are hard to diagnose.

text: When overriding a base-class or framework method, ensure the override name exactly matches the base class API; typos silently create a non-overriding method. If the override only needs a small transformation of inherited behavior, call super().<method>(...) instead of copying the parent implementation.
reason: Exact method names make overrides effective; delegating to super() avoids duplicated base logic and drift when parent behavior changes.
common_pattern: Subclass/framework method overrides should correctly integrate with base-class behavior: match the base method exactly and reuse inherited logic via super() instead of duplicating it.

text: Use single quotes for Python string literals (e.g., 'text'), switching to double quotes only when the string itself contains a single quote.
reason: Maintains consistent quoting style across the codebase and avoids unnecessary escaping when a single quote appears inside the string.
common_pattern: Both generalizations require using single quotes for Python string literals to maintain the project's consistent quoting style, with an exception for strings containing single quotes.

text: When duplicating a template block for a new tier/level, update all user-visible text (headings, labels, titles) to match the new tier, not just the conditionals and context variables. For example, in fundraising tier templates under djangoproject/templates/fundraising/, the heading text for each corporate membership tier block must match the tier key used in its {% if corporate_members.<tier> %} condition.
reason: Copy-pasted blocks frequently update the condition and variable references but leave the visible label text unchanged, producing headings that mislabel the content (e.g., 'Platinum' heading for diamond members), which misrepresents the sponsor's contribution.
common_pattern: When duplicating a template block for a new tier/level, ensure all user-visible text (headings, labels) is updated to match the new tier, not just the conditional logic and variable references.

text: In compound boolean conditions, order checks from cheapest/most local to most expensive, placing simple property comparisons before DOM queries or other expensive operations to exploit short-circuit evaluation.
reason: Prevents unnecessary expensive operations when earlier cheap checks fail, improving runtime performance.
common_pattern: Structuring boolean logic for clarity and efficiency: prefer direct/composed boolean expressions over unnecessary branching or indirection, and order compound-condition operands by cost to exploit short-circuit evaluation.

text: Keep PR changes scoped to the intended purpose; revert unrelated changes such as whitespace-only edits, formatting changes, trivial wording changes, and drive-by modifications. Dependency/package removal unrelated to the PR's stated purpose should be handled in a dedicated issue or PR.
reason: Unrelated changes add review noise, complicate approval, obscure the real intent, increase merge conflict risk, and can cause regressions; bundling unrelated cleanup with a focused change also makes review harder and obscures the rationale for the removal.
common_pattern: Maintaining focused, consistent, and noise-free diffs in PRs: avoid unrelated changes, and when introducing a new convention, apply it uniformly.

text: Remove CSS/SCSS declarations, selectors, and rules that do not affect rendered output — including values matching a property's initial/default, declarations always overridden by the cascade or specificity, selectors already matched by another listed selector, rules that cannot be tied to a reproducible rendering issue, orphaned selectors that no longer match any markup, and empty `@include`/directive blocks left behind after removing an element or its last declaration. Keep a rule only when it actually changes the rendered result (or is intentionally overriding, providing a fallback, or needed for specificity).
reason: Dead or redundant CSS adds maintenance burden, misleads future maintainers about how elements are actually styled or themed, can cause unintended theme-override side effects, and orphaned/empty rules add noise and falsely suggest styling is still applied.
common_pattern: Avoid dead, redundant, or no-op CSS/SCSS: remove declarations that do not change rendered output (match defaults, are always overridden, duplicate an already-matching selector, or are inert without prerequisites), and clean up orphaned/empty rules left behind by other changes.

text: Centralize CSS in the project SCSS stylesheets (e.g., `djangoproject/scss/_style.scss`) and apply styles via classes; do not add inline `style` attributes, inline `<style>` blocks, or page-specific duplicated CSS. Reuse existing shared styles before creating new ones. Prefer eliminating duplicated values that must be manually synchronized between SCSS files under `djangoproject/scss/` and HTML/templates (e.g., a CSS width matching an `img` width); if the duplication cannot be removed, add matching comments at both the SCSS and HTML/template sites that explicitly reference the counterpart file and selector/attribute.
reason: Keeps styling centralized, reusable, and consistent across the site; prevents duplicated CSS and scattered presentation logic. Cross-file value coupling is fragile, so editors changing one side must either remove the dependency or be clearly warned about the paired value at both locations.
common_pattern: CSS organization and class hygiene in djangoproject.com: centralize styles in project SCSS/shared stylesheets, use only defined/reusable classes, avoid inline or dead/legacy styling, and scope shared-style changes safely.

text: When implementing keyboard shortcuts, detect the correct platform-specific modifier key (`event.metaKey` for Command on macOS, `event.ctrlKey` for Ctrl elsewhere) and ensure it matches the UI hint; format keyboard-shortcut hints in UI strings using platform-native notation: on Apple platforms, use the modifier symbol followed by a narrow no-break space (U+202F) and the key without a plus sign (e.g., `⌘ K`); on non-Apple platforms, use `Ctrl + K`.
reason: Prevents shortcuts from silently failing or mismatching the displayed hint, matches platform conventions (Apple HIG), and avoids awkward line wrapping.
common_pattern: Platform-appropriate and consistent keyboard shortcut implementation and display in UI

text:
In `djangoproject/templates/aggregator/ecosystem.html` (and template-rendered resource/ecosystem list entries formatted as `Name — Description`), format every resource/package/community list entry as a single-line item `

      ` section (e.g. Third-party Packages, Package Communities, External Communities). The description must be a complete descriptive phrase (typically starting with an indefinite article), with the first word after the em dash capitalized and ending with terminal punctuation, matching the style of surrounding entries. Do not use placeholder list items that represent a category instead of a direct link.
reason: Consistent, self-contained `<li>` entries keep the ecosystem list scannable, reviewable, and correctly categorized while giving users direct, actionable links to each resource, and sentence-style descriptions keep visually parallel list items consistent and readable.
scope: file: djangoproject/templates/aggregator/ecosystem.html; also template-rendered resource/ecosystem list entries formatted as `Name — Description`
common_pattern:
All five generalizations describe the same convention for list entries in `templates/aggregator/ecosystem.html`: each entry must be a single-line `
  • Name — Description.

text: Keep migration history intentional and minimal: only commit migration files that correspond to a deliberate change in the PR; fold/squash unreleased or mergeable migrations into the preceding migration instead of adding new numbered files; and do not include migrations in PRs unrelated to the schema change (e.g., a linter-config-only PR).
reason: Incidental or redundant migrations add unrelated schema churn, obscure the intent of a PR, lengthen migration dependency chains, and are hard for reviewers to attribute to a deliberate model change.
common_pattern: Django migration best practices — managing the content, naming, purpose, and PR-scope of migration files so migration history stays intentional and clean

text: In Django templates using i18n, include {% load i18n %} and wrap every user-visible string (labels, buttons, headings, placeholders, ARIA labels, prose) in translation tags. Use the canonical {% translate %} tag (not the legacy {% trans %} alias) for short strings. Use {% blocktranslate trimmed %} for multi-line or interpolated strings, placing template variables inside the block rather than appending them after a {% translate %} string; in text/plain email templates, do not use the trimmed option (newlines are visible) and insert only intentional line breaks. In {% blocktranslate %}, only include a with clause for attribute lookups, filters, or renamed variables; omit it for simple variables. If a variable needs a filter, apply the filter in the with clause and reference the resulting variable inside the translated block. Reuse existing translation strings rather than hardcoding or duplicating msgids.
reason: Django's translation system only processes strings wrapped in translation tags; {% translate %} is the canonical tag, and {% blocktranslate trimmed %} keeps multi-line/interpolated messages intact for translators. Reusing strings avoids duplicate msgids. Text/plain emails differ because newlines render literally, so trimmed must be omitted there.
scope: Django templates using i18n (with text/plain email exception)
common_pattern: Django template internationalization (i18n) conventions: wrap all user-facing text in translation tags, prefer the canonical {% translate %} tag over {% trans %}, and handle interpolated/multi-line strings with {% blocktranslate trimmed %} and appropriate variable binding.

text: Format Django templates consistently: use a single space inside template tag delimiters (e.g., `{{ variable }}` and `{% block name %}content{% endblock %}`) with no missing or extra spaces inside braces; keep markup balanced and indented consistently by closing all HTML tags opened inside `{% block %}` containers and indenting standalone template output expressions to match the containing block level without unintended extra indentation.
reason: Consistent spacing matches standard Django template syntax style, while balanced markup and block-level indentation improve readability and prevent layout/CSS selector breakage or unintended rendered whitespace.
common_pattern: Django template formatting and markup style conventions

text: Avoid duplicating Django template content: assign repeated expressions once with `{% with name=value %}` (keyword-assignment syntax, not legacy `{% with value as name %}`); because `{% with %}` variables are scoped to the enclosing `{% block %}`, define values needed across multiple blocks in the view context (or a context processor) instead. Consolidate repeated markup blocks (e.g., loops, language/hreflang link tags, messages-rendering blocks) into a single shared loop, a reusable partial rendered via `{% include %}`, or a shared base/layout template, and only pull shared boilerplate into a page when that page actually needs it.
reason: Reduces repetition and keeps repeated values/markup consistent, so a change only needs to be made in one place, while avoiding dead template code and drift between duplicated blocks.
common_pattern: DRY principle applied to Django templates: avoid duplicating template markup, inclusion tags, or template files by parameterizing existing tags and factoring repeated fragments into shared partials/includes.

text: In Django templates, build internal links with named URL reversing tags—`{% url 'namespace:route' %}` for same-host routes, `{% host_url %}` when host-aware links are required, and `{% url 'document-detail' ... %}` for Django documentation—instead of hardcoding paths or absolute URLs. Append anchor fragments directly to the reversed URL output (e.g. `{% url 'members:teams' %}#code-of-conduct-team` or `href="{{ url }}#fragment"`); do not concatenate hardcoded path segments or precompute the combined URL with `add`/`{% with %}`. When using `document-detail`, keep the `url` parameter as the canonical document path.
reason: Multiple PRs converge on avoiding hardcoded Django template links by using URL names, with a consistent sub-pattern for appending section fragments directly to the reversed URL.
common_pattern: Django template link construction should use named URL reversal rather than hardcoded paths or absolute URLs, append fragments directly to reversed URLs, name URL variables descriptively, and render URLs as clickable anchors.

text: Keep all lines within the project's configured maximum line length (e.g., E501 via flake8/black/pre-commit, ~80 chars for legacy JS). When lines exceed the limit, wrap long expressions, string literals, HTML fragments, chained method calls, and test assertion messages using parenthesized implicit string concatenation, multiline strings, or by extracting the string into a variable — do not use backslash continuations. When a string literal fits within the line-length limit on a single line, write it as one literal rather than implicitly concatenating adjacent string literals across lines. Enforce line-length policy through the linter/formatter configuration, not through code-transformation or upgrade tools.
reason: Long lines fail automated pre-commit lint/formatting checks and block CI, and force horizontal scrolling in review. Linters/formatters are the correct place for style enforcement; wrapping methodologies (implicit concatenation, multiline strings, extracted variables) are more readable and maintainable than backslash continuations. Unnecessary adjacent string concatenation adds visual noise and makes the string harder to search for and translate, so a single literal is clearer when it already fits on one line.
common_pattern: Adherence to the project's configured maximum line length: wrapping long constructs when they exceed the limit, and only splitting strings when actually necessary for that limit.

text: For styling, use purpose-specific CSS classes rather than bare HTML element selectors. In templates, only apply CSS classes that are defined in the project stylesheets or actively used by JavaScript; remove unused, undefined, legacy, or copied-in classes from other contexts.
reason: Purpose-specific classes avoid unintended styling of all elements of that type, make styling intent explicit, and reduce coupling to HTML structure. Applying only defined or actively used classes avoids dead or misleading markup, prevents unintended layout side-effects from stale classes, and keeps templates understandable.
common_pattern: CSS organization and class hygiene in djangoproject.com: centralize styles in project SCSS/shared stylesheets, use only defined/reusable classes, avoid inline or dead/legacy styling, and scope shared-style changes safely.

Correct semantic use of HTML heading elements in templates: using headings (not

text: Do not create custom Django management commands that merely wrap or duplicate an existing built-in command; use the built-in command directly with its supported options (e.g. `dumpdata` with `--exclude` and `--indent`).
reason: Built-in commands are maintained by Django, reduce custom code and maintenance burden, and typically already provide the needed behavior through standard options.
common_pattern: Correct/proper usage of Django management commands — avoiding misuse, string-based flag parsing, and redundant wrappers instead of leveraging built-in behavior directly.

text: In navigation/pagination markup, use minimal semantic HTML: apply layout classes directly to the semantic container (e.g. `<nav>`) rather than adding a wrapping `<div>`; place links for simple navigation groups directly inside `<nav>` instead of `<ul>`/`<li>`; use a `<span>` for non-interactive current-page indicators instead of an `<li>`. For current/active links, omit `href` and mark the current item with `aria-current="page"`; do not add `class="active"` or redundant `aria-disabled="true"`. Style current states in CSS with semantic selectors such as `a[aria-current]` or `a:not(:link)` rather than `.active`.
reason: Combines the two complementary navigation-markup rules: minimal semantic containers/list markup and semantic current-page state. The shared principle is to use the semantic element/attribute that already fits the job instead of redundant wrappers, list markup, or presentational classes.
common_pattern: Semantic, minimal HTML for navigation/pagination: express state through ARIA/link semantics, style from that state, and avoid redundant presentational classes, wrappers, or unnecessary list markup.

text: Implement version-format predicates using semantic numeric threshold comparisons (e.g., `self.major >= 2028`) rather than string-length or digit-count heuristics (e.g., `len(str(major)) == 4`).
reason: Digit-count checks encode representation details rather than version semantics and can misclassify arbitrary version numbers used in test fixtures.
common_pattern: Django's calendar-versioning migration (PR#2733): documenting and implementing the mapping between the old A.B/A.B.C scheme and the new YYYY/YYYY.N scheme. Three related but distinct sub-patterns: (1) release documentation must map old↔new formats by release type at matching granularity, (2) version-format predicates should use semantic numeric comparisons, and (3) predicates should be named after the versioning scheme, not the current cadence.

text: When a Django GeneratedField or SearchVector expression needs a row-specific config value, pass the model field via F("config") into the expression term instead of enumerating all possible values with Case/When; expression builders that accept a config parameter generally accept resolvable expressions.
reason: SearchVector accepts a resolvable config, so using F("config") is simpler, avoids a large branch expression, and delegates per-row resolution to the database/framework.
common_pattern: Defining Django GeneratedField/SearchVector expressions in docs/models.py: prefer simple resolvable F expressions over Case/When enumeration for per-row config, and document any non-obvious expression workaround with an inline comment and reference link.

text: When a breakpoint value is derived from another breakpoint in SCSS, express it with CSS calc() rather than Sass arithmetic (e.g. calc(#{$breakpoint} + 220px) instead of $breakpoint + 220px).
reason: calc() is valid plain CSS and evaluated at runtime, whereas Sass arithmetic compiles to a fixed value and is less portable.
common_pattern: SCSS responsive breakpoints should be defined as centralized, semantically named variables rather than hardcoded pixels, and any value derived from another breakpoint should be expressed with CSS calc() instead of Sass arithmetic.
